claims.text: Systematically varying individual-element percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will produce measurable changes in mechanical properties.
The resulting mechanical-property changes will be predictable.
Composition changes affect mechanical properties by altering microstructural characteristics.
Composition changes affect mechanical properties through solid-solution strengthening.
The baseline HfNbTaTiZr alloy is near-equiatomic.
The baseline alloy has a homogeneous, predominantly solid-solution microstructure.
Arc melting can be used to synthesize high-entropy alloys.
Arc melting followed by homogenization can be used to prepare a controlled HfNbTaTiZr compositional series.
Changing individual-element concentrations changes lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing individual-element concentrations changes phase stability in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changes in lattice distortion and phase stability may affect grain structure.
Changes in lattice distortion and phase stability may affect precipitate formation.
Changing individual-element concentrations changes the degree of solid-solution strengthening.
Changes in lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening modify yield strength and hardness.
Mechanical properties will vary nonlinearly but systematically as individual elemental percentages are changed from the equiatomic baseline.
The effects are expected to hold only over limited compositional deviations.
Excessive compositional changes may cause secondary-phase formation or phase instability.
Secondary-phase formation or phase instability could obscure the direct mechanical contribution of individual elements.
X-ray diffraction can assess phase structure, and scanning electron microscopy can assess grain and phase morphology.
Failure to observe significant or systematic mechanical-property changes and expected microstructural modifications would falsify the hypothesis.
